1239. Maximum Length of a Concatenated String with Unique Characters

You are given an array of strings arr. A string s is formed by the concatenation of a subsequence of arr that has unique characters.

Return the maximum possible length of s.

A subsequence is an array that can be derived from another array by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

Example 1:

Input: arr = ["un","iq","ue"]
Output: 4

Example 2:

Input: arr = ["cha","r","act","ers"]
Output: 6

Constraints:

  • 1 <= arr.length <= 16
  • 1 <= arr[i].length <= 26
  • arr[i] contains only lowercase English letters.
output_format: Integer representing maximum length of valid concatenated string.
constraints: arr[i] contains only lowercase English letters
explanation: This problem can be solved using backtracking with bitmasking. Each string is converted into a bitmask representing characters present. If a string contains duplicate characters, it is discarded. Then we iteratively combine masks ensuring no overlapping bits. For every valid combination, we count the number of set bits to compute length. This ensures optimal exploration of all subsequences while efficiently checking uniqueness using bit operations.
